h1: Circular cold saws — manual, semi-automatic and automatic
intro: A cold saw cuts metal with a slow-turning, coolant-flooded circular blade instead of a hot abrasive disc, leaving a square, burr-free end that is cool to the touch and ready to weld. NovoTech sells two kinds in Canada, each on its own page: cold saws — the manual and semi-automatic circular saws of the fabrication shop: ISITAN SFC pull-down and semi-automatic saws with 10-3/4 to 13-3/4″ blades and NovoTech's value-line CS, PDS-315H and PDS-400 saws with 9 to 16″ blades, with abrasive cut-off saws and roller stands; and automatic cold saws — production saws that feed, cut and count by themselves: the CSM CT325 with servo feed for tube and bundles to Ø4″, the Bekamak BMDO XS carbide saws for solid bar to Ø6-1/4″, the BMDO CS HSS saws and the OPUS 300 for solid bar to Ø11-3/4″. Below, the two kinds compared, every model in one table, the buying guide and the questions we get asked; every machine comes with a CSA-approved panel and support from Mississauga, ON, Canada.

faq.q: Manual, semi-automatic or automatic — which do I need?
faq.a: By the number of cuts. For a few cuts a day in a fabrication or maintenance shop, a manual cold saw — the operator pulls the head down — is the simplest machine; a semi-automatic saw runs the cut from a foot switch with a regulated head descent, for batches of the same part. When the same lengths are cut by the hundred, an automatic cold saw feeds the bar with a servo gripper, clamps, cuts and counts by itself. The manual and semi-automatic saws are on the cold saw page, the production saws on the automatic cold saw page.

faq.q: TCT carbide or HSS cold saw?
faq.a: A carbide (TCT) blade runs at 130–920 ft/min and is the fastest way to cut solid steel bar in production — the Bekamak BMDO XS saws and the Ø11-3/4″ OPUS 300 are built around it, with servo feeding and a magazine loader for unattended runs. HSS blades run slower (22–130 ft/min on the BMDO CS) and are the choice for tube, thin walls and mixed work; the XS saws accept HSS blades for tube as well.

faq.q: What voltage do these machines run on?
faq.a: Three-phase machines are supplied for 600 V as standard with a CSA-approved panel; 208 V, 240 V and 480 V 3-phase are available on request, and 240 V single-phase on models whose main motor is 2.2 kW (3 HP) or less — a machine with a motor above 2.2 kW must run on three-phase power and cannot be converted to 240 V single-phase. Manual machines have no electrics.
